entries.clue: One leaving railway’s delayed convert (9)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the one departs, so I is taken out of the word

blocks.note: TRAINS (railway's, as in 'trains are') with I (one) removed

annotation.surface: A commuter grumbles that the railway is late again.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'railway's delayed' as 'trains late', then let the I leave. 'Convert' sits at the end looking like part of the railway story, but it means to change one language into another.
annotation.definitionFit: To translate is to convert words from one language into another.

entries.clue: Note: backward, dense and lacking courage (5)

indicatorNotes.backward: the next word is read from the end, so DIM turns round

blocks.note: ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A put-down describing someone as slow, stupid and cowardly.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Note' look like a heading, but it is the sol-fa note TI. 'Dense' means dim, not thick with matter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fearful, shy person is short of courage.

entries.clue: With child, filled with love etc (3,2,2)

indicatorNotes.filled with: something filled with a thing holds it inside, so SON is filled with O

blocks.note: love = nil = O, from tennis scoring

annotation.surface: A pregnant woman brimming with love and all the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With child' reads as one phrase meaning pregnant, but each word does its own job. Love is O from tennis, where a nil score looks like an egg (l'oeuf).
annotation.definitionFit: Etc, et cetera, is read out as 'and so on'.

entries.clue: Auction is small beer (4)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A modest drink on offer at an auction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small beer' is an idiom for something trivial, but here the two words work separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an auction is one kind of selling event, where goods go to the highest bidder.

entries.clue: A cat finds something very small (4)

blocks.note: the usual name for a male cat

annotation.surface: A cat discovers a tiny thing, perhaps a mouse or a crumb.
annotation.walkthrough: The cat is a tom, not a moggy or puss; the surface's tiny find is exactly what the answer is.
annotation.definitionFit: An atom is the classic example of something extremely small.

entries.clue: Go in and force open business (10)

blocks.note: to enter is to go in
to prise is to force open with a lever

annotation.surface: A burglar's instructions: go in and break open the premises.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a break-in, so 'business' reads as the shop being burgled; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a firm or commercial venture is a business.

entries.clue: Get rid of former private equity leaders initially (5)

indicatorNotes.leaders initially: take the first letter of each of the words private, equity and leaders

blocks.note: first letters of Private Equity Leaders

annotation.surface: A call to oust the former bosses of a private equity firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is both one of the words and part of the indicator, so its own L is included.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of pupils thrown out of school or air forced from the lungs.

entries.clue: Look cracking and sensational (3-7)

blocks.note: to eye is to look at
popping = cracking, bursting with a snap

annotation.surface: A rave review of something that looks superb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as British slang for excellent, but here it means making a sharp sound, like popping.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something sensational makes your eyes bulge in astonishment.

entries.clue: Express dissent for examination (7)

annotation.surface: Students objecting to an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link joining definition to wordplay, but it supplies PRO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to object publicly, by marching or complaining, is to express dissent.

entries.clue: Attractive object many announced with character (9)

indicatorNotes.announced: said out loud, so the word is spelt to match its sound

blocks.note: loads = many, spoken it matches lodes

annotation.surface: Describes a charismatic thing that many people have praised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' means magnetic, not good-looking: a lodestone is naturally magnetised rock.
annotation.definitionFit: A lodestone is a naturally magnetic stone, so it literally attracts.

entries.clue: Motorhead fiddle playing is unexceptional (6-2-3-4)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters are played with, rearranged

annotation.surface: A verdict that the heavy metal band Motörhead's violin playing is merely ordinary.
annotation.walkthrough: Motörhead were a loud British heavy metal band, the opposite of middle-of-the-road, which makes the surface's verdict comic.
annotation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road means moderate and unremarkable, unexceptional.

entries.clue: Condemnation of revolting disposition (4)

indicatorNotes.revolting: revolt as in turn round, so the word is turned back to front

annotation.surface: Someone's nasty temperament earns public censure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting, but it means turning over.
annotation.definitionFit: Doom is a judgment or sentence, an old sense of condemnation.

entries.clue: Wild rhinoceros not greeting singers (8)

indicatorNotes.not: the greeting is left out of the letters

annotation.surface: A wild rhino that doesn't say hello to the choir.
annotation.walkthrough: Remove HI from RHINOCEROS before shuffling what remains.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Bing Crosby and Frank Sinatra, who sang soft sentimental ballads, are the type.

entries.clue: Concealed disadvantage in promotional material for bird (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the snag sits in the leaflet, so its letters go inside the leaflet's word

blocks.note: a catch is a hidden snag
a flyer is a promotional leaflet

annotation.surface: Small print hiding a drawback in an advert for a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concealed' looks like the container instruction, but it belongs to the definition of the snag; 'in' does the placing.
annotation.definitionFit: A flycatcher is a small bird that catches insects in flight.

entries.clue: Completely destroy old book, set on fire by European judge (10)

annotation.surface: A European judge orders an old book burned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb, to rate or assess, not the person in court.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to wipe out so that no trace remains is to destroy completely.

entries.clue: Worker left bare mangled bicycle part (9)

indicatorNotes.mangled: BARE is mangled, its letters rearranged

blocks.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

annotation.surface: A worker abandons a stripped, wrecked bike component.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' is L, not the past tense of leave.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the bar a rider grips to steer is a component of the bike.

entries.clue: Books tough rugby players (9)

blocks.note: backs are the rugby players behind the scrum

annotation.surface: A bookie takes bets on hard-nosed rugby players.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' reads as a verb, as in booking players, but it is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Hardbacks are books bound in stiff covers.

entries.clue: Regularly plant Pinot in courtyard (5)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

blocks.note: P-l-A-n-T-P-I-n-O-t: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

annotation.surface: Gardening advice: keep planting Pinot vines in the courtyard.
annotation.walkthrough: Pinot is a grape variety, which makes 'plant' look like gardening advice.
annotation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved courtyard beside a house.

entries.clue: Barrel I carried containing heirloom (5)

indicatorNotes.containing: the answer is contained in the run of letters

annotation.surface: Someone lugged a barrel with a family treasure inside.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to find a word for barrel; the letters themselves hold the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: an object surviving from the past and handed down through a family is an heirloom.

entries.clue: Support associate according to the law (7)

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or chair

annotation.surface: Backing a colleague as the law requires.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Support' and 'associate' both look like verbs; they are nouns, LEG and ALLY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adverb from 'legal' means by law, lawfully.

entries.clue: Suggest annuities wrongly distributed (9)

indicatorNotes.wrongly distributed: the letters are handed out in the wrong order

annotation.surface: An allegation that pension payouts were misallocated.
annotation.walkthrough: An annuity is a yearly payment, often a pension, so the surface is a financial scandal.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to hint slyly at something unpleasant is to suggest it without saying it outright.

entries.clue: Very old worker hiding one hundred from Spain (7)

indicatorNotes.hiding: to hide something is to keep it inside you, so the worker's letters wrap round the number

blocks.note: the worker ant, a crossword favourite
cien is Spanish for one hundred

annotation.surface: An elderly labourer concealing a Spanish sum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One hundred' tempts you to C, but 'from Spain' asks for the Spanish word, CIEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: belonging to the distant past, like ruins or civilisations, is being very old.

entries.clue: Caused X to follow live attempt by head of technology (8)

indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come after, so X's letters go at the end, behind everything else
indicatorNotes.head of: take the first letter of technology

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist
X is the Roman numeral ten

annotation.surface: A tech chief's live trial made X, perhaps the social network, happen.
annotation.walkthrough: X comes first in the clue but last in the answer: 'to follow' sends it to the end. 'Caused' is a past participle, like begotten, as in 'the trouble it has caused'.
annotation.definitionFit: Begotten is the past participle of beget, to cause or bring about.

entries.clue: Swindle turncoats (4)

indicatorNotes.turn: the coats are turned round, MACS read backwards

blocks.note: read as TURN + COATS; macs are raincoats

annotation.surface: Accusing traitors of a con.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turncoats' splits into TURN and COATS; a mac is a British word for a raincoat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, informal: a dishonest scheme to cheat people out of money.

entries.clue: Melodic sounds upset number in charge (5)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

annotation.surface: An unhappy boss listening to tunes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like unhappy but tips SUM over.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: sounds arranged into melody and harmony are what we call by that name.

entries.clue: Alien getting unwrapped suit into case (4)

indicatorNotes.unwrapped: the outer letters are unwrapped, leaving the middle

annotation.surface: A space alien squeezing into a suit.
annotation.walkthrough: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and the like, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-regular word: a small ornamental holder for needles, pins or cosmetics is a kind of case.

entries.clue: Flipping crazy to follow a man (4)

indicatorNotes.to follow: the flipped word comes after A

annotation.surface: An exasperated remark about being driven mad by a man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, but it reverses MAD. Adam is the first man in Genesis.
annotation.definitionFit: Adam was the first man in the Bible, so he can stand for man.

entries.clue: Indifference of adolescent herds on the move (15)

indicatorNotes.on the move: herds on the move shift position, so the letters shift into a new order

annotation.surface: Teenagers roaming in packs, not caring about anyone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's teenage indifference is exactly the answer, a close fit between wordplay and meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Coldheartedness is a lack of feeling or sympathy, indifference.

entries.clue: More devious killer taking out American (5)

indicatorNotes.taking out: taking something out of a place removes it, so the named letter is removed from the killer's word

annotation.surface: A cunning assassin eliminates an American target.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking out' sounds like a killer's work; here it removes the A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the comparative: craftier, more cunning.

entries.clue: Mysterious giant mice getting agitated (9)

annotation.surface: Strange oversized mice becoming restless.
annotation.walkthrough: The giant mice are a comic image; their letters, not the rodents, make the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means mysterious and hard to interpret.
